title: Microsoft Unveils AI Model Based on Qwen
key_facts: Microsoft launched Microsoft-Decision-1, a model for routing, classification, prioritization, data verification and workflow management, based on Alibaba's open Qwen3.5-9B model.

Unlike text-generating language models it gives structured answers: it assigns calibrated probabilities to a fixed set of options (yes/no, multiple choice, ratings) and can score AI responses and agent actions against set criteria.

Microsoft says it achieved the highest accuracy across 36 benchmarks covering nearly 150,000 questions not used in training, and was the fastest tested: 2.5 times faster than H2O-Lightning-4B v1.1 and 35 times faster than GPT-6 Sol.

Microsoft says the same query reworded eight ways changed the decision in 1.3% of cases on average; in security tests with 5,250 queries from 11 benchmarks it rejected malicious actions while keeping utility.
Microsoft's Xbox Research used it to annotate more than 10,000 reviews from surveys, Steam and X, at quality comparable to GPT-6 Sol, more than 14 times faster and at 200 times lower cost.
The Copilot team used it to assess chatbot and agent responses, matching GPT-5.6 Luna at a hundredfold speed.
In Microsoft Discovery it evaluated experiments for adaptive replanning, with 46 times more stability than LLMs at three times the speed.
Usage costs $0.042 per million input tokens and output tokens are free; Microsoft plans to adapt the approach to other foundation models, including its own MAI and OpenAI's.
quote_evidence: Microsoft has launched Microsoft-Decision-1, a model designed for routing, classification, prioritization, data verification, and workflow management.
It is based on Alibaba’s open Qwen3.5-9B model.

why_it_matters_hint: A small, cheap model that scores options could let companies automate many routine AI checks at far lower cost, on Microsoft's own numbers.
